question: What is the main goal of disease surveillance in a rural maternity center?

options.A: To replace the need for routine antenatal booking registers
options.B: To audit the financial expenses of the maternity clinic
options.C: To calculate the monthly salaries of community health workers
options.D: To act as an early warning system against maternal and neonatal infections

explanation: Surveillance tracks health data continuously so facilities can spot unusual illness patterns early before they spread widely. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of these describes active surveillance?

options.A: Proactively searching for cases by visiting community leaders and birth attendants
options.B: Waiting for sick patients to walk into the maternity clinic
options.C: Reviewing old delivery records stored in the facility archive
options.D: Submitting monthly summary forms at the local government headquarters

explanation: Active surveillance means health workers take the initiative to seek out hidden or unreported cases instead of waiting for them to appear. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h1)

question: What event usually signals the start of a potential outbreak in a clinic?

options.A: The retirement of the senior nursing officer in charge
options.B: An increase in the total number of normal antenatal care visits
options.C: The annual delivery of routine vaccines to the health facility
options.D: A sudden cluster of patients presenting with identical unusual symptoms

explanation: When multiple patients present with similar symptoms in a short time frame, it points toward a common source or outbreak. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h2)

question: What should you do FIRST when an outbreak is suspected in a maternity center?

options.A: Stop all documentation in the patient health registers
options.B: Begin immediate infection containment measures without waiting for lab results
options.C: Close the facility permanently and lock all maternity ward doors
options.D: Wait for international health agencies to visit before taking any action

explanation: Waiting for definitive test results can allow an infection to spread rapidly, so immediate containment is necessary. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is strict visitor restriction important during a maternity ward infection outbreak?

options.A: It reduces the physical movement of pathogens into and out of the ward
options.B: It lowers the monthly electricity bill of the health center
options.C: It ensures that family members complete their antenatal education
options.D: It prevents relatives from cleaning the delivery room instruments

explanation: Restricting visitors cuts down the pathways by which infectious agents can enter or leave the clinical environment. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is required when transporting biological samples from a rural clinic to a reference laboratory?

options.A: Maintaining proper cold chain storage using ice packs in vaccine carriers
options.B: Exposing the specimen containers directly to bright tropical sunlight
options.C: Adding strong chemical bleach directly into the diagnostic sample tube
options.D: Placing unlabelled sample tubes openly inside a standard handbag

explanation: Many biological samples degrade quickly without proper temperature control, making cold chain transport essential for accurate results. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h4)

question: What happens if a clinical specimen is collected and handled improperly during an outbreak?

options.A: It simplifies the paperwork required for the final outbreak report
options.B: It automatically accelerates the recovery rate of the affected patients
options.C: It may yield false results and misdirect the public health response
options.D: It increases the financial allocation sent by the federal government

explanation: Bad samples lead to incorrect lab conclusions, which can cause health teams to chase the wrong diagnosis and waste resources. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h4)

question: Who is the primary local officer a rural midwife should notify immediately upon suspecting an outbreak?

options.A: The international news media network representatives
options.B: The Local Government Area Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer
options.C: The commercial transport union chairman in the nearest city
options.D: The national minister of finance and economic planning

explanation: The DSNO is the designated official responsible for coordinating local public health responses and reporting alerts up the health system. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why is it necessary to involve traditional and community leaders during a rural health outbreak?

options.A: To build local trust and encourage community cooperation with containment measures
options.B: To approve the architectural design of the maternity center building
options.C: To collect personal income taxes from households in the village
options.D: To replace the clinical duties normally performed by trained midwives

explanation: Community leaders hold significant influence, and partnering with them helps dispel fear so the population follows vital health instructions. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of an after-action review following an outbreak?

options.A: To evaluate what went well and identify areas to improve future preparedness
options.B: To punish staff members who caught the infection during work hours
options.C: To increase the cost of maternity services for incoming pregnant women
options.D: To permanently close down the maternity center due to past failures

explanation: An after-action review is a learning session that helps health teams strengthen their systems for the next potential health threat. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which activity is essential during the post-outbreak recovery phase in a rural clinic?

options.A: Refusing to admit any new pregnant women for at least two years
options.B: Transferring all existing clinical staff to a different state
options.C: Destroying all past patient registers so no records remain
options.D: Restocking depleted emergency medical supplies and repairing equipment

explanation: Outbreaks consume vast amounts of consumables and drugs, so recovery requires replenishing stocks to keep the clinic functional. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T3#BMP316_U1_T3_h6)
